chunks: Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Aban ibn Uthman, from one of our companions, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him)

Regarding the man who gives Dirhams as advance payment for foodstuff for a term. The foodstuff is released (delivered), but he (the seller) says: 'I do not have foodstuff with me, but look at its value, so take its price from me.' He (peace be upon him) said: 'There is no problem with that.'

key_terms.إِسْلَامُ: Advance payment (giving money in advance for goods to be delivered later)
key_terms.الطَّعَامِ: Foodstuff (general term for food in this context)

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling if a seller receives advance payment for food but cannot provide the specific food item later?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi clarifies the permissibility of substituting the physical delivery of foodstuff with its cash value when the seller lacks the specific goods, resolving a practical nuance in the contract of 'Islam' (advance payment for goods). It highlights the flexibility in Shia jurisprudence regarding the fulfillment of deferred obligations, allowing monetary settlement as a valid alternative to in-kind delivery when the original item is unavailable. This ruling underscores the principle that the core obligation is the provision of value, accommodating market realities within the framework of riba-free trade.
